Hashing the Seed Data Too

The seed script's placeholder passwords become real hashes, using the exact same function register uses.

prisma/seed.js's four seeded users have carried the same literal string — 'placeholder-not-hashed' — since Lesson 2. Leaving it as-is now would mean none of them could actually log in: verifyPassword('password123', 'placeholder-not-hashed') would just fail, since that string was never produced by bcrypt.hash in the first place.

// Figure 4.2: real hashes in the seed data (prisma/seed.js, excerpt)
import { hashPassword } from '../src/utils/password.js';

const DEV_PASSWORD = 'password123';

async function main() {
  // ...existing deleteMany() cleanup...

  const hashedPassword = await hashPassword(DEV_PASSWORD);

  const [customer1, customer2, agent1, admin] = await Promise.all([
    prisma.user.create({
      data: { name: 'Casey Customer', email: 'casey@example.com', password: hashedPassword, role: 'customer' },
    }),
    // ...the other three users, same hashedPassword...
  ]);
}

Every seeded user shares one hashedPassword, computed once — there's no reason to hash 'password123' four separate times when the result is identical, and reusing it keeps the seed script's own output simple: whichever seeded account you log in as, from the customer to the admin, the password is the same password123, printed by the script's own final console.log as a reminder. This only works at all because prisma/seed.js imports the exact same hashPassword from utils/password.js that auth.controller.js's register endpoint uses (next topic) — one function, two callers, no chance of the seed data and a real registration ending up hashed two different ways.
